correctness.rationale: In the specified cubic graph a named proper coloring is an ordered partition into three perfect matchings. An independent implementation (not executing or loading the frozen verifier/certificate) constructed the graph from the LCF offsets, enumerated 42 perfect matchings, 20 factorizations and 120 named states, and traversed each bichromatic two-factor to exhaust the moves. Every switch changes a nonempty set of edges, and its activated pair and support distinguish it from other moves out of the same coloring. There are two 60-state components, each with 162 edges and degree counts 54 at five and six at nine; the supplied base-graph automorphism exchanges them. Since all bichromatic cycles have length six or eighteen, each switch flips the local color-permutation sign at three or nine vertices on one fixed side of the bipartite base graph, so the product sign changes. All-source distances reproduce the spheres (1,5,17,25,12) and (1,9,27,21,2) for the two degrees, radius and diameter four, and pair counts (162,540,738,330) in each component. Canonicalizing the palettes and removing loops gives two ten-state windmills, each with one universal vertex and three disjoint triangles upon deleting it. The Finding uses three individually named edge colors; incidental wording about six vertex colours in the limitations is not the mathematical definition.
residual_risks: The proof is for the specified finite graph and moves; metric values apply only to pairs in the same named-color component.

evidence: The 2017 result gives general triangle-freeness for the named Kempe graph, not Pappus-specific self-centered radius four. The 2012 planar bipartite cubic graph theorem does not supply this instance.
The 2021 bipartite census gives an aggregate distribution of class counts, not the Pappus transition graph or its metric.
broader_coverage.reasoning: These broad theorems and census results do not cover the full metrics on their own. The demonstrated coverage comes instead from the Pappus-specific published exact data.

evidence: The palette action is free and commutes with Kempe switches. Swapping each entire alternating cycle on a listed representative and applying each palette permutation to both endpoints exhausts all 324 named edges in the 120 lifted states without assigning colors or searching for factorizations.

All-source BFS of the lift gives both order-60 components and exactly the frozen sphere multiplicities and distance counts. A standard adjacency-preserving permutation search on the earlier edge list yields, for example, the sector-exchanger (0,1,2,13,12,17,16,9,8,7,14,15,4,3,10,11,6,5). Bipartiteness also follows directly from the previously published six- and eighteen-cycle profiles and the sign argument.
claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: This is not a reconstruction from quotient adjacency alone, which discards switch-label information. The previous certificate's complete representatives and full edge list recover that information by the deterministic move rule; the remaining metric calculation asks for standard data of an already specified finite lift.

At order 18 the 2021 Table 2 is aggregate (149 connected bipartite cubic graphs, with maximum 16 classes), not an indexed Pappus two-class metric entry. The linked dataset is described as containing maximum-class graphs and code; the files were not accessible in the lawful retrieval attempts.
exact_database_or_table.reasoning: The exact Resultary certificate is the decisive table, not an inference from the uninspected census files. The measured Pappus count is two, not the maximum described by the supplement link.

originality.rationale: The October 26 Resultary record 81d0af0022f9 already states the exact palette quotient for the same graph and moves, including its two windmills and its two cycle profiles. It expressly does not claim a theorem about the all-named graph, but its earlier certificate supplies the ordered graph edges and all twenty canonical color words. These data determine the full named graph by a direct palette lift, with no fresh coloring enumeration. I lifted that certificate: from one representative per orbit, swap each cycle before normalization and take all six translates of each resulting edge. The two components, bipartition and complete distance data follow by ordinary BFS on the lift. A standard adjacency-preserving permutation search of the same supplied base graph also gives a component-exchanging isomorphism. Thus the quotient is explicitly covered and the remaining narrow named-state statistics are mechanical readouts of the earlier exact data; they are not asserted to be explicit in the earlier theorem's text.
residual_risks: The inaccessible census supplement could contain more explicit data, and literature naming conventions can hide other examples. Neither uncertainty is used as evidence against originality; the decisive prior certificate was available and the lift was checked.

value.rationale: The named/unnamed distinction and the different metric geometries on a canonical cubic graph are mathematically meaningful. As a proposed new exact result, however, the frozen contribution combines an already stated quotient with routine expansion and metric computation from its earlier complete configuration certificate. No additional structural theorem or otherwise nonmechanical invariant survives this comparison.
residual_risks: This does not rule out value in a different theorem for a larger graph family or a conceptual theory of these lifts; neither is claimed here.
